steps.title: COUNT per name
steps.prompt:
GROUP BY bundles rows into piles that share the same name.
Then count(*) works on each pile.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, count(*) FROM customers GROUP BY name;
hints: Start with SELECT name, count(*).
FROM customers.
Finish with GROUP BY name.
Write: SELECT name, count(*) FROM customers GROUP BY name;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, count(*) FROM customers GROUP BY name;
steps.memory_trick: GROUP BY = one output row per pile.

steps.title: Just the name pile (Brahim Belkadi)
steps.prompt: HAVING filters the piles after they are built - WHERE filters rows before.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, count(*) FROM customers GROUP BY name HAVING name = 'Brahim Belkadi';
hints: Build the piles with GROUP BY name.
Add HAVING to keep one pile.
The test is name = 'Brahim Belkadi'.
Write: SELECT name, count(*) FROM customers GROUP BY name HAVING name = 'Brahim Belkadi';
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, count(*) FROM customers GROUP BY name HAVING name = 'Brahim Belkadi';
steps.memory_trick: WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters piles.
